    Elvish Leaf¶

    [!INFO] Measured Like a Forest Grows — Patient and True The living measure of Elves — not struck in metal but grown in gardens. A leaf, a branch, a bowshot — patient enough to outlive empires.

    Base Units¶

    Elvish measure is famously unstandardized on purpose. Each elven refuge keeps a Mother Tree whose leaves are the local standard; an Elvennrin oak leaf is 11.2 cm, an Elvenkrad silver-leaf is 9.8 cm. Elves consider this correct — measure should remember where you are. Human merchants despair. Elves consider that correct too.

    Domain Unit Relation Notes
    Length Seed base oak acorn length ~ 2.5 cm
    Leaf 4–5 Seeds the Leaf — Mother Tree leaf, 9–12 cm. Local leaf = local truth
    Span 8 Leaves hand-span (~80 cm) — weaver's unit
    Ell 2 Spans forearm to fingertip + leaf
    Pace 2 Ells walking step ~ 1.6 m
    Bowshot 120 Paces ~192 m — distance a war-bow carries true. Battlefield standard
    Longbow 2 Bowshots 240 Paces — legend distance
    Canopy 10 Bowshots ~1.92 km — forest canopy walk
    Grove 10 Canopies ~19.2 km — between Mother Trees. Elvish league
    Weight Acorn base one acorn
    Leaf-weight 40 Acorns ~ 50 g — apothecary weight
    Branch 12 Leaf-weights ~ 600 g — basket herb weight
    Bough 10 Branches ~ 6 kg — sack measure
    Burden 10 Boughs ~ 60 kg — what one elf carries on a long walk
    Volume Cup base carved acorn cup ~ 40 mL
    Bowl 12 Cups ~ 480 mL
    Jar 8 Bowls gourd jar ~ 3.8 L — ferment, oil, rainwater
    Barrel 10 Jars ~ 38 L — cellar barrel

    The joke: asked how far to the next glade? an elf answers three Bowshots, or one song. Both are correct for an elf.

    Time and length blur in Elvish: a Grove is both distance and the walk between two Mother Trees at contemplative pace (~4 hours). Dwarves demand conversion tables; elves offer tea.

    Who Uses¶

    The Elven peoples — Elvennrin (Central Erisdar), Elvenkrad (North Erisdar), the Tree Tribe (Lumina), Great Cattos elven enclaves, and the diaspora in Loren and Magna. Also favored by herbalists, bowyers, and garden-architects across Erisdar: if you buy Elvish linen, it is measured in Spans, not Yards, and it is always generous.

    The Elvennrin bowyers certify Bowshots by firing from the Mother Tree at the proving ground — if the arrow falls short, the Bowshot is redefined, not the bow.

    Conversion Notes¶

    • To Erisian Standard: 1 Elvish Pace ≈ 1.75 Erisian Yards (elves stride long). 1 Bowshot (120 Paces) ≈ 210 Erisian Yards. 1 Grove ≈ 12 Erisian Miles. Conversions are advisory — elves will not swear to a Grain.
    • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Span ≈ 2.85 Dwarven Stone — dwarves call the Span sloppy. Elves call the Stone stunted.
    • To Trade Routes: Caravan masters carrying elf-cloth convert Spans to Erisian Yards at 0.88 : 1 and add 5% leaf-tax for re-cutting.
    • Romanium: Elves weigh Romanium — when they must — in Leaf-weights, but prefer to price it in years of keeping. A Romanium ingot is not sold in many groves; it is entrusted.

    Flavor¶

    Elvish measure is companionable, not coercive. A length includes the time you spend enjoying it. An elf who says the city is two Groves away means you will walk through two forests, notice the light, perhaps nap, and arrive when you should. Humans who demand in miles, exactly are gently asked why they are in such a hurry to leave a forest.

    Elven apprentices learn measure by growing: you are given an acorn, a leaf, and a bow. When you can hit the leaf at a Bowshot with the acorn still in your palm, you understand distance.

    The Shadows engineered hatred of elves partly because an unstandardized, patient measure cannot be taxed efficiently — and inefficient taxation is anathema to empire.
